prerequisites: It is recommended to have partially achieved the learning objectives established in the following second-year courses: Programming Technologies and Paradigms, Human-Computer Interaction, and Databases, as well as third-year Software Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to select, design, deploy, integrate, evaluate, build, manage, exploit, and maintain hardware, software, and network technologies within appropriate cost and quality parameters.
Ability to select, deploy, integrate, and manage information systems that satisfy organizational needs, with identified cost and quality criteria.
Ability to conceive systems, applications, and services based on network technologies, including the Internet, web, e-commerce, multimedia, interactive services, and mobile computing.
Analyze and prepare system requirements by interacting with a client, producing the functional requirements part of a tender request.
Analyze, evaluate, and discuss different alternatives for implementing, developing, and subcontracting a software system, selecting the most appropriate for the organization's needs.
Perform technical reviews of products developed by other work teams.
Prepare and monitor an implementation and deployment plan for a software system.
Prepare a software configuration management plan and control versions and changes.
Prepare the strategy and integration tests for a software system.
Understand the content and objectives of different process, evaluation, and quality model standards applicable to software products and processes.
Understand different enterprise architecture models and their relationship with involved technologies.
Understand the different functionalities of typical packaged applications (CRM, ERP).

syllabus_topics: General process of elicitation, validation, and implementation of requirements
Requirements extraction and acceptance criteria in agile methodologies (SCRUM)
Quality and Standards in Software Engineering
General concepts. Definition and Types. Standards
Software Testing. Test design. V-model (levels and types). Automation.
Software Configuration Management. Plans, Version Control (Git), and Changes
Enterprise Information Systems. Architecture and functionalities.
Realization of an Information Systems project using SCRUM. Kanban board, Definition of User Stories, Implementation, Version Control, and Testing.

assessment_methods.method: Student work in classroom practices and deliverables
Continuous and formative evaluation in laboratory practices
Evaluation of student contribution during the course in laboratory practice reports and products, and final presentation

assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The final grade is calculated as 0.65 * Practices + 0.35 * Theory. If the minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary assessment, if the ordinary grade is not 'Not Presented' and is at least 5.0, those grades can be carried over. Otherwise, the theory block is evaluated by a written exam (minimum 5.0), and the practical block by an individual assignment (minimum 5.0). The grading formula is the same as for ordinary assessment, with the same rule for not meeting minimums.
